visual_match: X-axis must be log-scaled and labeled with the number of random features N, ranging from at least 10^1 to 10^4 and covering the training sample size n≈300 with a vertical dashed line at N=n
Y-axis must be log-scaled and labeled 'Test risk (squared loss)' and display values between ~10^-2 and 10^1 consistent with the paper's risk range
Both train and test risk curves must be present: train risk reaches zero (or near‑zero) at N≈n and stays at zero for N>n, test risk shows a peak near N=n and declines for larger N
The overall shape of the test curve must be U‑shaped for N<n, a clear peak at N≈n, and a descending tail for N>n, matching the caption description
scientific_claim: The reported test risk curve must exhibit a local maximum at N within ±5% of the training sample count n (i.e., 285≤N≤315)
For N>n the test risk values must be statistically lower (e.g., at least 10% reduction) than the peak risk at the interpolation threshold
The test risk at the smallest N (≈10) must be higher than the risk at the largest N (≈10^4), confirming a double‑descent pattern
implementation: Code must generate Random Fourier Features using z(x)=cos(Wx+b) with W drawn from N(0,1) and b uniform on [0,2π)
Linear regression must be solved via minimum‑norm least squares (e.g., using numpy.linalg.pinv or sklearn.LinearRegression with fit_intercept=False and no regularization)
Training set must be a random subset of exactly 300 samples from sklearn.datasets.load_digits, with one‑hot encoded targets for squared loss

Prediction must be obtained by applying the linear model to test features and computing squared error against one‑hot targets; classification error may be reported via argmax but must not be used to compute the plotted risk
budget_use: The entire experiment (data loading, feature generation for all N values, model fitting, risk computation, and figure generation) must complete within 300 seconds on a single CPU core
The sweep over N must include at least 15 logarithmically spaced points between 10 and 10^4, ensuring sufficient resolution to observe the peak
Memory usage must stay below 2 GB; code must not pre‑allocate arrays larger than this limit
integrity: All plotted points must be derived from actual model training and evaluation; no hard‑coded risk values or copying of expected curves are allowed
Figure annotations (vertical line at N=n, legends, axis labels) must be generated programmatically, not manually edited after plotting
The code repository must include the full execution log with timestamps, showing start and end times and confirming wall‑clock compliance
